Mike King.bio: Founder of our Open. Early 3x champ, All-VVC center on the gridiron for the Gilman Owls. Failed spelling at GHS.

Mark Oakley.bio: Folks from Tuscola have a screw loose—Oak got some decent wiring. New knees find him clicking and possibly adding to his major resume. Oak and Harry Caray: they don’t spend money, they abuse it (Jimmy Piersall).

Mike Maher.bio: The GOAT in every respect. Duck only married Mickey for Mig. 18x—many think he is done (is there a Jack in the future?). Good man to know if you need a grill—just don’t have him deliver it.

Stu Miller.bio: Early 2x champ and a co-Owl in the GHS class of '78 with Duck (note: Willie didn’t graduate). Splitting the fourth quarter between Florida and Wisconsin.

Mark Hasty.bio: We were so blessed when Dogg and Rae joined the tour. Rae is short for “radar” — the ball is always going in the hole, especially on chips and putts. Trust but validate—Chinese proverb.

Scott Dillon.bio: Named himself after taking a "10"/“Moose” on a hole. Underachiever best describes his golf résumé; overachiever in life. True.

Jeff King.bio: Formerly known as Chief, Oll's official secretary of the Open. Would rather golf than do anything else in the world. Also known as Pipeline for straight drives.

Patrick King.bio: Son of Duck and the first lefty on the Tour. Named after the neighbor's cat from Oll and Duck's childhood in legendary Gilman, Illinois.

Jay Pettit.bio: Blood relative of Mig, with early success on the Tour and two major championships to prove it. A true Geneseo Maple Leaf, born and raised, who is now building all the houses in town.

Cary Bottorff.bio: Youngest of the Owl clan, with a view of the Gilman Ditch from his patio growing up—no doubt molding him into the man he is today.

Chris Baum.bio: Cam truly introduced golf to the EIU Panthers on the Tour—Thomas Hall, 1979. Always been a fair-weather fan; a loyal one he’s not. Good to remember.

Ryan Gillespie.bio: Named after the football player RGIII (not believed to be related). Cousin of Mig and Jay by blood, and Duck not by blood. He has learned that the Oll Open starts on the back nine on Sunday.

Bryan Amidon.bio: Oak's son-in-law and a California native. Always smiling and improving exponentially since moving to Illinois.

Mark Widdel.bio: The long drink of water with a smile a mile wide. Critical advice: if you want to play well tomorrow, don’t have Wood pour your drinks today.

Theo Hoby.bio: Morton Potter and lifelong friend of FiFi, Duck, and Bloomer. Generally runs a little late but arrives with a lot of pop in that simple lefty swing.

Ryan Blum.bio: Former Potter relocated to the desert sun of Arizona. Underachiever in the Open to date (2026). Last chance in ’26, as marriage follows in ’27. The End—pun intended.

Tom Thornton.bio: Geneseo native whose adult life has been in Florida, heading north for his inaugural Open. Mystery game—no information available. Excited to see what kind of stick Tom brings.

Steve Koch.bio: New to the Open, but a lifelong player from Oak Park Fenwick. BSS Tar with Duck and God. No swearing around Steve and Duck. Thank you in advance.

Mitchell Bottorff.bio: Butsy's son and another young player improving every round. Bears lover with Dad and W—all others are fake (fact). When consistency hits his bag, watch your wallets.

Ted Duke.bio: Ollie's friend from the grocery days—Oll on meat and Ted on lettuce. A wonderful man with an even more wonderful short game; Ted would get up and down in the jungle. Fact.

Mark Murray.bio: Don't blink or the ball is in the air. Tuscolaite and EIUite. Oak and CB share the Tuscola heritage—you can only shake your head when listening.

Tom Oberwetter.bio: Close your eyes and listen—hear the laugh? Best laugher in the world and another famous EIU alumnus. A swing smoother than a cat's <you know what>.

Bob Vogrich.bio: Another Owl who generally makes the annual trek for the Friday round. Vog was one of the very few who studied at Gilman High School—shame on him.

Rick Shields.bio: World is short for the World's Most Interesting Man. Befriend him, as he controls the world—for example, he has diverted rain from the Open on multiple occasions. Retired and playing more, so watch out.

Tom Gerdes.bio: We lost him too young; he was only 47 years old. The Open was Dude's scene—being with friends, laughing, and playing golf (horribly if he was in Duck's group). RIP Dude—we love you!

Darin Smith.bio: Excellent golfer who ran into health issues too young and no longer physically plays, but is always with us in spirit. Extremely knowledgeable and destined to be Duck's caddie in our next life.

Tom Fine.bio: Dude's best friend from Springfield—a great addition to the Open who played until Dude's passing. Dude, Puff, and a full cooler: there was nothing better.

Mike Matthews.bio: The Voice of ISU and a great stick. Forbidden from winning; permanently withdrew after Duck nearly rolled the cart down the bluff on number 12 at Weaver, then walked the next three or four holes.

Tom Seeforth.bio: Now in Louisville, making it hard to get back for the Open. Moose was de-invited in the early years to make room for Weed (true story). The boom of his dynamite will always echo in Open history.

John Sherman.bio: Son of Oak and Tracy—another long drink of water with a beautiful swing. Limited appearances, but hopefully more in future years.

Timmy Miller.bio: One of Stu's boys from Chicago. They make an occasional trek down for a day of the Open, and it is always wonderful to have the old guard's offspring playing.

Michael Miller.bio: One of Stu's boys from Chicago. They make an occasional trek down for a day of the Open, and it is always wonderful to have the old guard's offspring playing.

Kevin Mueser.bio: Played many of the early years of the Open, with a sweet swing and an even sweeter demeanor. A wonderful friend who still sticks his head in occasionally at the Open.

Jordan Mueser.bio: Mue's son and a strong stick in high school. Played a few Opens—too good to qualify for W—then moved away for college and thereafter. A lot of fun memories with Gordo and Mue.

Bryan Berndt.bio: College friend of Jay from Pekin, hence the nickname creatively coined by Duck. Friday only in these early years — hopefully more in the future.

Jim Shepard.bio: Shep played in the early years. The only barefoot player in Open history—and maybe golf history—with a picture to prove it. An excellent player who introduced a few of us to Lick Creek, a good memory.

Kevin Eimen.bio: Kayk is short for cake eater, as he was in college during his early years of the Open. A Gilman native whose adult life in Colorado has made it difficult to play in the Open.

Zach Freeman.bio: Woody's son-in-law and an occasional visitor to the Open to play with the long drink. A very nice young man, a lefty, and hopefully a player with more Open rounds in his future.

Rob Ginder.bio: Moose's brother-in-law was in town for one Open and played—good stick! Ginders like golf and an occasional drink. Great people!

Greg Bange.bio: Homer native—another interesting hometown. Only played a few Opens but is a frequent Orlandoer and the best storyteller in history. Have Banger tell you about Leo from Homer if you run into him.
